newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS - Gengold rises out of tough Q1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Gengold rises out of tough Q1.

text.p: Shrugging off a dismal bullion price and the effect of fewer shifts worked, Gengold Ltd on Monday raised distributable income for the three months to end-March 1997.

Rising above a grim forecast for the industry's first quarter gold results -- due to a near seven percent lower rand gold price and the Christmas holiday disruption -- Gengold announced a profit of 87.7 million rand compared to 68.9 million rand in the preceding quarter.
Conceding it had been a "tough" quarter, managing director Tom Dale attributed the profit in part to a Beatrix Mines Ltd tax rebate and the cancellation of consulting fees at Evander Gold Mines Ltd.
But Evander's capital spending for the quarter was lower and it also raised gold production.
"We've got some encouraging results," Dale said.

"Against a background of negative sentiment and grim forecasts for both the gold and gold equity markets, Gengold increased distributable income for the seventh consecutive quarter, generating twice the cash of the March 1996 quarter a year ago," the mining house said in a statement.
Beatrix received 20 million rand from its final 1995 tax assessment, raising pre-capital spending net income to 88.62 million rand from 75.87 million rand.
Evander won 25 million rand from the cancellation of its consulting services agreement with Gencor Ltd.
Overall, it was the star performer in Gengold's stable, swelling pre-capex net income to 41.58 million rand from 34.99 million in the December quarter.

Despite fewer shifts due to holidays -- Gengold's mines officially worked 67 shifts in the March quarter compared to 71 in the December quarter -- Evander increased tonnes milled to 874,000 from 850,000 and gold output to 4,930 kg from 4,792 kg.
The company's results were further brightened by Gengold's announcement it could exploit ore below existing infrastructure at Evander's Winkelhaak No 6 shaft without a rights issue.
Evander could one day also exploit three million ounces of recoverable gold in its Poplar project areas, at a cost of 120 million rand, Gengold announced.

Hedging assisted Beatrix in countering lower production -- 3,777 kg versus 3,844 kg -- and an 8.7 percent increase in working costs by delivering a gold price of 52,507 rand/kg which was 791 rand higher than the average spot price in the quarter.
Dale said the hedge gold price for Beatrix in the current June quarter would be just slightly less than 53,000 rand/kg.

The hedge was implemented to fund the No 3 shaft project. Dale said the project was "significantly ahead of schedule" and Gengold did not anticipate the earlier expected funding shortfall there of 170 million rand.

St Helena Gold Mines Ltd posted a fall in pre-capex net income to 7.42 million rand from 9.30 million, largely cut by the lower gold price received which dropped to 50,674 rand/kg from 55,873 rand/kg.
Nevertheless, the company continued to generate funding for its Oryx division which saw capex rise to 85.97 million rand from 80.68 million rand in the preceding quarter.
St Helena is likely to see a capital recoupment in the June quarter due to the sale of certain assets, Dale said.
